metadata.title: A tree characterization one vertex above the Bougard-Joret counterexample boundary
metadata.description: We prove that for every integer k at least 3, the minimum number of edges of a k-connected graph on 2k vertices with independence number k-1 equals k squared. We characterize every extremal graph using a nonstar tree on k+1 vertices and independent missing-neighbor fibers of sizes degree minus one. The numerical extension beyond previously identified ranges begins at k=4; k=3 is a known consistency case. The proof includes the exceptional two-surviving-tree-vertices connectivity case. Exact finite controls include all nonisomorphic trees on 4 through 9 vertices, independent cut and max-flow verifiers, and a complete labeled order-six census. Das and Gupta retain priority for the original Bougard-Joret disproof and preceding boundary classification. This preprint does not resolve the full revised first regime or second regime, and has not been peer reviewed.
